rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Specific latent heat** L is the heat to convert 1 kg across a phase change at constant temperature: $Q = mL$ — for water $L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg (fusion) and $L_v = 2.26\times10^6$ J/kg (vaporization). Both are measured by calorimetry. **Ice method:** $mL_f + mc_wT = (m_wc_w + m_cc_c)(T_2 - T)$.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Q = mL; L_f = 3.34×10⁵ J/kg; L_v = 2.26×10⁶ J/kg - Steam: mL_v + mc_w(100−T) = (m_wc_w + m_cc_c)(T−T₂) - Ice: mL_f + mc_wT = (m_wc_w + m_cc_c)(T₂−T)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Steam's two-step release:** L_v on condensing at 100 °C, then mcΔT cooling to the final temperature — both sides of the balance.  ·  **Dry ice matters:** surface water on ice adds hidden mc terms.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A sieve or trap keeps water droplets out of the steam.  ·  Crush the ice so it finishes melting before the room undoes the experiment.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2021*** — 5 g steam into 50 g water (30→50 °C): L_v = 6.3×10⁵ J/kg from the given data.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: measurement of specific latent heat of fusion, vaporization (within Quantity of Heat).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Physics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Copy the worked example and hide the result until the last step.  ·  Name the unit of every term in the formula.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Two heat terms per phase change: mL + mcΔT."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (4m): 30 g of ice at 0 °C is added to 150 g of water at 25 °C. Final temperature 10 °C (neglect calorimeter). Find L_f.** — Gained: 0.03L_f + 0.03×4200×10 = 0.03L_f + 1260. Lost: 0.15×4200×15 = 9450. → 0.03L_f = 8190 → L_f = 2.73×10⁵ J/kg.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Practise the 5m balance twice: once steam-side, once ice-side.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The 5m steam numerical (NEB 2021)** is the canonical calorimetry-with-phase-change problem.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Q = mL; L_f = 3.34×10⁵; L_v = 2.26×10⁶ J/kg (standard values).  ·  Steam method: mL_v + mc(100−T) = gained; Ice method: mL_f + mcT = gained.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Refrigerators exploit L_f: freezing water absorbs 3.34×10⁵ J/kg inside the freezer box.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Melting ice dropped into warm water absorbs → B  ·  Wet ice makes the calculated L_f → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Measuring the Hidden Heat Latent heat cannot be read on a thermometer; it must be *weighed out* in energy balances. Drop melting ice into warm water, or pass steam through it, and calorimetry converts temperature changes into L_f and L_v — the numbers behind refrigeration, steam engines and weather.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2021) ### 2.1 Specific latent heat of fusion and vaporization - **Specific latent heat of fusion ($L_f$):** heat required to convert 1 kg of a solid to liquid at its melting point, with no temperature change. Water: $3.34 \times 10^5$ J/kg.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 52:** these measurements quantify the latent heats defined there. - **To Topic 51:** the same calorimetric balance with an added mL term. - **To engineering:** L_v powers steam engines and refrigeration cycles (compression/condensation).
